Journal/Date: Cancer & metabolism (2016)

--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: The role of anaplerotic nutrient entry into the Krebs cycle via pyruvate carboxylase has been the subject of increased scrutiny and in particular whether this is dysregulated in cancer. Here, we use a tracer-based NMR analysis involving high-resolution (1)H-(13)C-HSQC spectra to assess site-specific label incorporation into a range of metabolite pools, including malate, aspartate and glutamate in the acute myeloid leukaemia cell line K562. We also determine how this is affected following treatment with the redeployed drug combination of the lipid-regulating drug bezafibrate and medroxyprogesterone (BaP).
[RESULTS]: Using the tracer-based approach, we assessed the contribution of pyruvate carboxylase (PC) vs. pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) activity in the derivation of Krebs cycle intermediates. Our data show that PC activity is indeed high in K562 cells. We also demonstrate a branched entry to the Krebs cycle of K562 cells with one branch running counterclockwise using PC-derived oxaloacetate and the other clockwise from the PDH activity. Finally, we show that the PC activity of K562 cells exclusively fuels the ROS-induced decarboxylation of oxaloacetate to malonate in response to BaP treatment; resulting in further Krebs cycle disruption via depletion of oxaloacetate and malonate-mediated inhibition of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) resulting in a twofold reduction of fumarate.
[CONCLUSIONS]: This study extends the interest in the PC activity in solid cancers to include leukaemias and further demonstrates the value of tracer-based NMR approaches in generating a more accurate picture of the flow of carbons and metabolites within the increasingly inappropriately named Krebs cycle. Moreover, our studies indicate that the PC activity in cancer cells can be exploited as an Achilles heel by using treatments, such as BaP, that elevate ROS production.

key_findings.finding: Direct AML evidence is concentrated in one primary study: PMID 27493727, “Malonate as a ROS product is associated with pyruvate carboxylase activity in acute myeloid leukaemia cells” (Cancer & Metabolism, 2016). In K562 AML cells, tracer-NMR showed high pyruvate-carboxylase (PC) activity; after bezafibrate/medroxyprogesterone (BaP), the authors report that PC-derived oxaloacetate fuels ROS-induced decarboxylation to malonate, with malonate-mediated SDH inhibition and an approximately twofold fumarate reduction.

source_tools.relevance: Primary AML paper abstract and extracted content directly state PC activity, ROS-induced oxaloacetate-to-malonate decarboxylation, and downstream SDH/fumarate effects.
Independent focused AML/PC search returned the same primary paper as the direct match.

key_findings.finding: Malonate is not itself a ROS molecule (it is a dicarboxylate metabolite/SDH inhibitor); the defensible interpretation of “malonate as a ROS product” is that ROS mediate its formation. In the AML study, ROS are the causative oxidants and malonate is the carbon-containing product, not the ROS species itself.

source_tools.relevance: AML primary study explicitly describes “ROS-induced decarboxylation of oxaloacetate to malonate.”

Oxidative-stress chemistry study shows H2O2/tert-butyl hydroperoxide decarboxylate oxaloacetate to malonate in chemical systems and rat mitochondria, supporting the product-versus-oxidant distinction.

key_findings.finding: The strongest non-AML mechanistic evidence links succinate/complex II to ROS generation, while malonate acts mainly as an inhibitor/probe: PMID 22689576 (JBC, 2012) showed complex II can generate superoxide/H2O2 during succinate-supported forward and reverse reactions, and malonate prevented this ROS production by inhibiting the flavin site. This does not show that malonate is generated from succinate.

source_tools.relevance: Primary mitochondrial study directly tests succinate-supported ROS and malonate inhibition.

key_findings.finding: A second AML-relevant primary study, PMID 40931045 (Leukemia, 2025), reported increased malonate in PML::RARα-positive acute promyelocytic leukemia cells and interpreted it as an SDH inhibitor affecting succinate-to-fumarate conversion. The available abstract/content does not establish ROS production, PC activity, or a PC–malonate link, so any connection to the 2016 K562 mechanism is inference only.

source_tools.relevance: Primary APL study reports increased malonate and SDH/succinate-fumarate context but its abstract does not link malonate to ROS or PC.

key_findings.finding: The oxidative-stress product literature provides non-AML support for ROS-associated malonate: PMID 16781453 (Free Radical Biology & Medicine, 2006) found peroxide-driven decarboxylation of oxaloacetate produced malonate, whereas oxidative stress also generated succinate from α-ketoglutarate. This supports ROS-mediated metabolite formation but is not evidence in leukemia cells and does not demonstrate succinate-derived malonate.

source_tools.relevance: Primary oxidative-stress study directly reports malonate formation from oxaloacetate and distinguishes it from succinate formation from α-ketoglutarate.

key_findings.finding: Reviews identified for context include PMID 35892689 (2022, “Succinate Dehydrogenase, Succinate, and Superoxides…”) and PMID 37508015 (2023, “Complex II Biology in Aging, Health, and Disease”), but the searches did not identify an additional review or primary AML study that independently demonstrates a malonate–ROS–PC pathway beyond PMID 27493727.

source_tools.relevance: Review-focused search identified these reviews and the direct AML study as the relevant evidence set.
